description:
## Project onto the completion event, NOT the job span

The job span covers only 2 of 5 completion sites. Measured: 0
`BuildBackendProduct` job spans in a real log, yet 3 `backend_program.defined`
events -- those completions happen span-less.

    drive.rs:452           span YES
    product_drive.rs:185   span YES
    compiler.rs:139        span NO
    jobs/native.rs:65      span NO
    jobs/macro_runtime.rs:65  span NO

All five route through `ExecutionContext::complete_job` (`drive.rs:29`), which
unconditionally emits `fz.compiler2.work_graph.applied` with `(&World,
&JobCompletion)` (`drive.rs:41`) -- verified exhaustively; no caller reaches
`World::complete_job` directly. That event is complete, needs no plumbing, has no
span-panic hole, and is simply NOT allowlisted (`jsonl.rs:797`).

Allowlist it and project onto it. Leave the job span for timing.

## The one engine change: stop discarding the wake cause

`Scheduler::complete` holds `fact_use` and the `shift` classification when it
wakes each reader (`scheduler.rs:395`) and drops both into a bare `Vec<J>`.

    pub wakes: Vec<Wake<J, F>>,   // replaces enqueued: Vec<J> + coalesced: Vec<J>
    struct Wake<J,F> { cause: FactUse<F>, job: J,
                       disposition: Enqueued|Coalesced, shift: bool }

`enqueue_dependents` already receives both; `enqueue_step` gains two parameters.
No new state -- strictly less discarded. `shift` distinguishes ascent-wake from
ground-shift-wake, which is fz-kdt.44's vocabulary, free.

Enqueued-vs-coalesced is agenda state that no fact movement can reconstruct,
which is why it must be carried rather than derived. This is the ticket's own
sanctioned exception ("carry the minimal typed cause with the agenda entry; do
not build a telemetry-only graph").

Cost, measured: `changed_revision_wake` is 1,433 for the main session of
00420_enum_take_drop_split (total sanctioned starts 2,593 = job span count), so
~1.4k transient `Wake` records per compile against a 660ms compile. Negligible.

Blast radius verified: `.enqueued`/`.coalesced` have NO production consumer --
21 + 2 assertions in `scheduler_test.rs`, plus `jsonl.rs:1255`/`:1374`. Rewrite
those assertions straight; do NOT add compatibility accessors, which would be a
test-only affordance on a production type.

## Also project, all already in hand

- exact changed output `FactKey`s (today `jsonl.rs:1251` writes `.len()`);
- `AppliedStep.movements` -- computed at `scheduler.rs:362`, never projected;
- `blocked` as keys, not kinds; `rebased`.
- Reads come from `world.work_graph.reads(&job)` at projection time
  (`Scheduler::reads`, `scheduler.rs:200`); `World.work_graph` is `pub(crate)`
  and `jsonl.rs` is in-crate. Nothing stored.

Note `movements` is built from a `HashSet` (`scheduler.rs:305`), so its
within-event order is a `RandomState` artifact. Fine for a multiset assertion;
say so in the docs rather than leaving it to be rediscovered.

## Red tests

TDD 1 (one changed fact, one unchanged conclusion) and TDD 2 (two coalesced
changes before one evaluation: both causes attributable without two evaluations).

## Docs with the code

`AppliedStep` is documented at `.agent/docs/fact-engine.md:380` and
`.agent/docs/telemetry.md:384`. Both change here, not in the last child.
title: Job causality: carry the wake cause, project onto work_graph.applied
